AI made the file. Why are you still uploading it?

Cinematic ad, live action. A tired developer at a desk at night repeatedly performs the same tedious loop: dragging a file from a folder to an email window, attaching it, sending, then doing it again with a slightly different file. Quick cuts, escalating rhythm, mild absurdist comedy of repetition. Frustrated sigh. Warm desk lamp against cool monitor glow. No readable text on screens, screens show only abstract blurred UI shapes.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic, live-action, medium shot of a tired developer (S1), a man in his late 20s with messy hair and dark circles under his eyes, sitting at a cluttered desk at night. The lighting is a high-contrast mix of a warm, orange-gold glow from a classic desk lamp on the left and a cool, pale blue light emanating from a large computer monitor on the right. The screen displays abstract, blurred UI shapes with no readable text. S1 reaches for the mouse and drags a blurred file icon from a folder window to an email window; as he clicks "send," a soft, digital "whoosh" sound is heard. [Shot 2] At 00:01.200, the camera cuts to a tight close-up of S1's hand on the mouse and the monitor. The action repeats faster: a drag, a drop, a click. The rhythmic sounds of the mouse clicking and the "whoosh" of the sent email accelerate. [Shot 3] At 00:02.400, the camera cuts back to a medium shot of S1. His expression is one of numb exhaustion. He repeats the drag-and-drop sequence with a slightly different blurred file, his movements becoming mechanical and frantic. [Shot 4] At 00:03.600, the camera cuts to an extreme close-up of S1's face. He freezes for a split second, then lets out a long, heavy, frustrated sigh, his shoulders slumping as his eyes stare blankly into the cool monitor glow. The camera shakes slightly to emphasize his internal agitation. [Shot 5] At 00:04.500, the camera cuts to a wide shot from behind the desk, showing S1's small silhouette against the dark room as he immediately begins the dragging motion once more, returning to the tedious loop.

overall_soundscape: The environment is quiet with a low, ambient electrical hum from the computer. Dominant sounds are the sharp, rhythmic clicking of a computer mouse and a repetitive, synthesized "whoosh" sound effect every time an email is sent. A loud, audible exhale of a frustrated sigh occurs near the end.

non_diegetic_music: A quirky, minimalist percussion track featuring a ticking clock sound and a pizzicato string pluck. The tempo increases steadily throughout the video, creating a sense of escalating tension and absurdist repetition, stopping abruptly during the sigh.

p: ["no product UI ever shown, only wordmark+tagline in final 2s","garbled/illegible file-explorer and email UI text in close-up upload shot","warped/distorted hand and fingers during reach gesture","generic corporate-office setting doesn't signal 'AI coding agent' audience","product only on screen for ~2 of 5 sampled frames"]

The pain-point headline is a strong scroll-stopping hook and the tired-office-worker visual sells the 'still uploading' fatigue, but the ad never shows what Artifact Share actually does—no artifact page, no URL, no comment/update loop—so it functions as a problem ad without a visible solution. The close-up screen insert meant to dramatize uploading is blurry with scrambled, unreadable text and a warped hand, which reads as an AI-video glitch rather than a real UI. Ending on a plain wordmark plus tagline over a silhouette is a weak, low-salience payoff for a product whose whole pitch is 'one URL'.

p: The paperclip icon reads as 'attachment,' not 'URL/link,' which muddles the core concept for a message that hinges on 'one URL.' Actors and office setting are generic corporate stock footage with zero developer/coding cues (no terminal, no code editor, no AI agent UI) despite the target audience being AI-coding-agent developers — this will not stop a dev scrolling X. The product itself only appears as a blurred, illegible mock UI in the final two frames, so viewers can't actually see what Artifact Share looks like or does. Text overlay does convey the message/CTA clearly and legibly, which is the ad's main strength.

s: insert into evaluations (id, created_at, creative_id, harness_version, hook_score, product_clarity, message_clarity, product_salience, cta_intent, visual_quality, artifact_score, overall_score, disqualified, failure_modes, critic_notes) values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
p: ["product never shown as a UI/demo, only as a text overlay of the domain name","metaphor shifts abruptly from digital file duplication (desktop folders) to physical paper clutter, muddying the 'version chaos' concept","jarring color-to-B&W cut between the folder-chaos beat and the payoff beat","stressed-actor stock footage carries the ad more than the product itself"]

The hook text (final_v2/v3/final/v7) is a strong, relatable pain point for developers, and the folder-multiplication frame sells absurdist chaos well. But the ad pivots to a generic stressed-office-worker-buried-in-paper cliché that has nothing to do with file versioning or coding artifacts, and the actual product is never demonstrated — it only appears as a text card reading the URL. A dev watching this would recall 'guy overwhelmed by paperwork' more than 'a tool that keeps one updating link,' which weakens both product salience and click intent.

p: 6-15s Punchy Loops with Bold One-Liner Hook

Short 6-15 second vertical or 1:1 video loops featuring strong opening motion or bold text in first frame, native dialogue or captions, optimized for X timeline ads. Used for B2B SaaS with 3-5x engagement vs statics.

if we apply 6-15s punchy loops with bold one-liner hooks on X, CTR improves because the format matches X's fast-scroll, muted viewing (80%+ sound off) and rewards quick visual hooks that stop thumbs in <3s while driving impressions/virality
Generate 1:1 master with AI tools like Seedance; burn in captions; test one-liners like 'Stop paying for tools that do this for free'; pair with 9:16 cutdowns
